correctness.rationale: All candidate leader pairs fall into one hub-rim orbit and floor(n/2) rim-distance orbits. The hub grounding gives a Toeplitz path inverse-square eigenvalue sum; an explicit positive Schur complement gives the exact rim-pair objective. For rim count 3..10, verify.py independently checks all 216 labelled pairs by exact rational matrix inversion and cross-checks the orbit formula. For n>=11, the Rayleigh quotient of the all-ones follower vector gives J_rim>= (n-1)^2/36; the nonnegative walk-series Green-kernel comparison gives J_hub<=3(n-1)/(5sqrt(5))<27(n-1)/100<(n-1)^2/36. Modal Lyapunov covariance for xddot+eta L xdot+Lx=noise is exactly L^-2/(2eta). Strict inequalities and ties are enumerated correctly; independent proof sources are not asserted.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible primary texts treat first-inverse leader selection (arXiv:1302.0450; arXiv:1412.6595) and do not state an inverse-square optimal pair classification on wheels. The explicit six-rim numerical reversal establishes that a theorem optimizing the first-inverse criterion alone cannot imply the present inverse-square winner. A second-order coherence study on trees is different in both graph and leader formulation. Targeted literature and published-finding corpus searches found no equivalent or strictly stronger stated theorem, subject to residual coverage risk.
residual_risks: Specialized inverse-square leader-selection results may be poorly indexed by title and search descriptions; absolute historical priority cannot be guaranteed.

A publicly available tree-network second-order paper was checked by abstract only and cannot be asserted absent on whole-text grounds; its stated tree-graph scope does not logically subsume wheel placement.

General optimization routines can calculate individual finite wheel sizes; the value claimed is the exact infinite-family phase classification and the first-versus-second moment reversal, not that the underlying inverse-square definition is novel.

value.rationale: The exact leader-allocation geometry of an infinite natural graph family changes between first-order and relative-damping second-order noise models. The theorem resolves all two-pair options for every rim count, with a strict six-vertex threshold, rational exact boundary witnesses and a uniform non-finite all-size proof. This is motivated design information beyond isolated numeric tables, and it gives a concrete counterexample to treating inverse and inverse-square coherence objectives as interchangeable. Restriction to unweighted wheels is explicit.
